title: The associated graded of a finitely generated ideal is finite type
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring and $J\subseteq A$ a finitely generated ideal. Then $\operatorname{gr}_J(A)$ [def-weil-pbc-associated-graded-ring], with its degree-zero $A/J$-algebra structure, is a finite type $A/J$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra].

source.place: Algebra, Tag 05GH (lemma-completion-Noetherian, lines 23022–23063), step 2 (finite degree-one generation)

proof.text: Choose a finite generating family f : Fin t → A of J. Let g_i be its degree-one classes and S the A/J-subalgebra generated by the finite range of g.
Every degree-one class belongs to S: induct on ideal-span membership using the finite generating family, additivity of the quotient inclusion, and the scalar formula for the associated graded.

Induct on n to show that the class of every x in J^n belongs to S. In degree zero this is the algebra map. In the successor step use J^(n+1)=J^n J and induction on ideal-product membership. Classes of products are products of classes, and sums are preserved.
Induct on the additive direct sum to conclude that S is the whole associated graded ring. The finite family g therefore witnesses finite type.
